newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: MONEY RATES STABLE IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: MONEY RATES STABLE IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: HARARE, July 1 (Reutetr) - Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted largely unchanged from their previous levels on Tuesday, dealers said.

The market opened short of 54.7 million, but liquidity was boosted with the maturity of Z$750 million worth of treasury bills and the central bank auctioned Z$600 million of 91-day bills at 24.99 percent.
The central bank paper was being traded on the secondary market at Monday's 24.75 percent and call money was also stable at 22 percent.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought steadily at 26 percent and sold at 25 percent while bankers acceptance bills were quoted at 25.5 (buying), also unchanged from Monday, but were a touch firmer at 24.85 from 24.75 percent on the sell-side.
